children: Kotak Institutional Equities retained its 'ADD' call on TVS Motor and 'SELL' rating on Bajaj Auto, raising their fair values to Rs 4,350 and Rs 9,600, respectively, as it expects strong two-wheeler export growth to continue through FY2027. TVS Motor was down 0.34% at Rs 4,036.30, while Bajaj Auto was up 0.53% at Rs 11,485 as of 11:32 am on Wednesday.

"We expect TVS to outpace Bajaj as incremental growth skews toward Africa, where TVS carries higher saliency," Kotak said in its India sector view. It expects two-wheeler exports to see a broad-based recovery across Latin America, Africa and Asia through FY2027, but trends to moderate from FY2028E "as pent-up demand exhausts and the higher base".

"2W exports have seen a broad-based recovery across LatAm, Africa and Asia over FY2025-27, driven by productive use demand in LatAm, a structural taxi economy and improvement in currency availability in Africa and a restocking-led rebound in Asia," the brokerage said.

Kotak has increased EPS estimates for Bajaj Auto and TVS Motor by 3-5% on higher export volume assumptions. It expects Latin American 2W industry growth to moderate to mid-single digits as "the cyclical support that drove the last three years fades", while Africa is expected to deliver high-single-digit CAGR as growth shifts to financing depth, electrification and localisation.

"Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh recovered as the balance of payments stress unwound and dealer stock normalized, releasing years of deferred replacement demand," Kotak said. It expects restocking-led markets to decelerate sharply as pent-up demand exhausts.

For TVS Motor, Kotak increased FY2027-29E EBITDA estimates by 2-5% on higher volume and ASP assumptions. "We expect its medium-term growth prospects to remain strong," led by EV 2W volumes, steady ICE demand and an improving brand franchise in export markets. It retains 'ADD' with a fair value of Rs 4,350, up from Rs 4,150.

title: Kotak retains 'ADD' on TVS, 'SELL' on Bajaj as 2W exports fire on all cylinders
